name: Prague
tagline: Fairy-Tale Architecture and Central European Charm at a Discount
description: Prague is one of Europe's most beautiful cities, with medieval architecture, a world-class beer culture, and a cost of living well below Western Europe. The city has excellent public transport, fast internet, and a growing international community. While it lacks the beaches of Southern Europe, Prague compensates with stunning seasons, incredible cultural offerings, and a central location that makes all of Europe accessible by train or budget flight.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day Schengen visa-free for US citizens. Long-term visa available for financially independent persons (proof of funds required). Zivnostenský list (trade license) also used for residency. Path to permanent residency after 5 years.
quickFacts.language: Czech, English widely spoken in Prague
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of Europe's safest capitals
quickFacts.climate: Continental with warm summers and cold, snowy winters

housing.description: Modest studio in an affordable, well-connected district (Žižkov/P3, Nusle, Vršovice)

dining.description: Occasional pub lunches and street food; a hearty daily menu runs ~180–230 CZK

healthcare.description: Required commercial comprehensive cover, entry level (PVZP, age 45–59)

transportation.description: DPP annual transit pass (3,650 CZK/yr ≈ 304 CZK/mo) across the metro/tram network

entertainment.description: Neighborhood pubs, occasional cinema, free parks and cultural events

1M.lifestyle: This is unpretentious, entirely comfortable Prague living. A tidy studio in a lively residential district puts trams and the metro minutes from the door, so no car is needed. Days mix home-cooked meals with the occasional 200-koruna pub lunch and a cheap, excellent Czech beer. Culture is free or nearly so — riverside walks, parks, and the city's endless architecture. Money is watched, but nothing essential is missing, and Prague's safety is a standout.

housing.description: Decent small 1BR in a nice district (Vinohrady edge, Karlín, Holešovice)

dining.description: Regular eating out — daily menus plus a few mid-range dinners each week

transportation.description: DPP monthly pass (550 CZK) plus occasional ride-hail

entertainment.description: Gym membership, cinema, concerts, and nightlife

2M.lifestyle: A step up into a proper one-bedroom in a district people actually want to live in — leafy streets, cafés, and a short tram ride to the center. Eating out becomes routine rather than a treat, a gym membership is a given, and there is room for concerts and a night out. Transit still covers almost everything, with a ride-hail when it is raining. This is settled, low-stress city life with a small margin for extras.

housing.description: Good 1BR in a desirable central district (Vinohrady, Karlín, Letná)

dining.description: Frequent quality dining — mid-range restaurants and specialty cafés

healthcare.description: Top-tier domestic comprehensive with pre-existing cover (PVZP Exclusive class)

entertainment.description: Gym, theatre and opera, concerts, an active social calendar

3M.lifestyle: The comfortable-independence tier. A good central one-bedroom in Vinohrady or Karlín means walking to dinner, the tram at the corner, and the Old Town twenty minutes away. Dining out several times a week is unremarkable, groceries lean toward quality and the farmers market, and there is a real budget for theatre, opera, and concerts. Health cover upgrades to a plan that includes pre-existing conditions. Nothing is stretched — this is Prague enjoyed rather than merely afforded.

housing.description: High-spec prime-central 1BR or small 2BR (Prague 1/2, Malá Strana, prime Vinohrady)

dining.description: Frequent fine dining, wine bars, chef's menus

healthcare.description: International expat health plan (Cigna Global Silver/Gold tier)

transportation.description: Transit plus heavy ride-hail and occasional car use (car enters as discretionary here)

entertainment.description: Premium gym, opera/theatre season tickets, events, hobbies

luxuryExtras.description: Club membership, fine wine, spa, concierge, and travel fund

5M.lifestyle: Prime-address living in the historic core or the best of Vinohrady, in a high-spec apartment with room to breathe. Fine dining and good wine are woven into the week, groceries come from the best delis and organic markets, and a weekly cleaner keeps things effortless. Health cover moves to an international expat plan for wider access and English-language care. A car becomes a discretionary convenience alongside the excellent transit, and there is a standing fund for spa days, clubs, and travel.

housing.description: Luxury 1–2BR at a prime address (Malá Strana, Old Town, Prague 6 diplomatic quarter)

healthcare.description: Premium global health plan (Cigna Global Gold/Platinum)

transportation.description: Private car (parking, insurance, fuel) plus ride-hail/driver as needed

entertainment.description: Box seats, private clubs, premium cultural and leisure experiences

luxuryExtras.description: Premium club, fine-wine cellar, concierge, spa, and a generous travel fund

10M.lifestyle: Uncapped Prague luxury. The address is one of the city's finest — a Malá Strana apartment beneath the castle or a villa-grade home in Prague 6's diplomatic quarter — with regular housekeeping and a concierge tier of service. Dining is at the city's Michelin tables as a matter of habit, the wine is cellar-grade, and culture means box seats and private-club events. A car and driver sit alongside first-class transit, and a large discretionary fund covers spa, clubs, and travel. This is the ceiling of what money buys locally, comfortably below the equivalent in a Western European capital.
